notes: inherent: The inherent vowel is typed 'a' inside a word and dropped at its end (ਘਰ ghar). Speech drops it inside words too (ਕਰਦਾ karda, ਸਮਝ samajh), and typists follow speech or the letters; the skeleton drops every a between two consonants so both give one key. addak: The addak ੱ doubles the consonant after it (ਪੱਕਾ pakka, ਬਿੱਲੀ billi, ਉੱਤੇ utte). The tables have no sign that spells the letter after it, so every addak + consonant is a key of `consonants` (two code points), spelled with the consonant's first letter doubled or, a fifth of the time, single; ਅੱਛਾ is achha or accha. The skeleton drops a doubled letter, so pakka and paka are one key. nasals: The tippi ੰ is n inside a word (ਪੰਜਾਬ punjab, ਮੁੰਡਾ munda), m before a labial (mb and mp fold to nb and np). The bindi ਂ ends many words and is typed n or not at all (ਨਹੀਂ nahin / nahi, ਮੈਂ main / mai, ਹਾਂ haan / haa), so optionalFinals names it: such a word is also keyed without the n. letters: ਸ਼ ਖ਼ ਗ਼ ਜ਼ ਫ਼ ਲ਼ are the consonant + nukta after NFC (U+0A33, 0A36 and 0A59-0A5E are composition exclusions), so their keys are two code points. ੜ is r or d (ਪੜ੍ਹਨਾ parhna / padhna). The virama is written only for the subscript letters ੍ਰ ੍ਹ ੍ਵ (ਪ੍ਰੇਮ prem, ਪੜ੍ਹ parh). ੈ is ai, ae or e (ਹੈ hai / he). ਏ after a vowel is e or ye (ਜਾਏਗਾ jaega / jayega). skeleton: Aspirates fold to their plain letters, sh and chh/ch to s and c, z to j, f to p, w to v, q to k; aa, ee and oo to a, i and u; ei to ai, then ai and ae to e (ੈ is typed ai, ae or e: ਪੈਸਾ paisa / pesa, so ੇ and ੈ words share keys and are told apart by ranking); mb and mp to nb and np; nm to m (ਨਿੰਮ nimm). An a between two consonants is dropped, and a final a after a consonant.
